── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 42, 46, 34, 41 mi
This week: 12 mi over 3 runs.
Body: "Legs came back by Thursday. Blister healed."
Feeling: "Itching to train again."
Asks: "I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Last week was followed exactly, with three easy runs and four rest days, and the marathon finished at about 3:50, five minutes over your target. …
Answers: (1) No, not yet, on both counts. Going to 40 miles would more than triple last week's 12 miles in one step, and the legs need a few more easy weeks before anything that stresses them. (2) What comes next for you: a 10K in late November, another marathon, or a break from racing for a while? Tell me the race and its date, and I will build the plan from there.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off, since the legs are still recovering from the marathon on Oct 18.
Tue: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 140, flat route. The first run back on a steady…
Wed: rest. A full day off between the two runs keeps the recovery real.
Thu: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 140. The second easy run of the week; keep the effort…
Fri: rest. A full day off before the weekend runs.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 140. Keeps the rhythm going without adding stress…
Sun: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 140, flat route. The longest run this week, still…
